Translations.Title: Reading scales with 2, 4, 5 or 10 intervals: Reason and Apply
Translations.Explanation: This Cambridge Primary Stage 3 supporting lesson develops the open DfE Year 3 ready-to-progress focus “Reading scales with 2, 4, 5 or 10 intervals”. A digit's value depends on its position. Compose and decompose numbers with place-value units, and use a number line or powers of ten to reason about magnitude. Reason and apply by selecting a representation, solving a contextual problem, and checking the result independently. The lesson is Edulytics-authored from OGL material; Cambridge remains the academic reference authority and no Cambridge objective wording is reproduced here.
Translations.KeyConceptsAndRules: Read and interpret scales divided into 2, 4, 5 or 10 equal intervals, including non-zero starting values.
Translations.WorkedExamples: Example A: A scale runs from 15 to 55 in 4 equal intervals. Each interval is 10, so two intervals after 15 is 35. Check four intervals reaches 55.
Translations.StepByStepSolutions: Find the interval value from the endpoints, locate the pointer by counting equal intervals, then verify the full scale span.
Translations.CommonMistakes: Do not compare numbers by looking at a single digit or by counting digits after the decimal point. Keep the value of each place explicit and check the size of the whole number. A correct-looking number is not enough if the representation or reasoning does not match the original relationship. Re-read the question and check units and magnitude.
